message.content:
This is a women's knit top of 84% modal, 9% cashmere, and 7% elastane. It is not a sweater, because the fabric has more than 10 stitches per cm, so it falls under T-shirts and similar garments in heading 6109 or 6110. Heading 6110 covers sweaters, pullovers, and similar articles, and CBP classifies garments with fewer than 9 stitches per 2 cm as sweaters. Here the stitch count is higher than that, and the garments are T-shirt style with a round neck and hemmed sleeves, so 6109 fits.

Heading 6109 covers T-shirts, singlets, tank tops, and similar garments, knitted or crocheted. The fiber is mostly modal, which is an artificial fiber, but the cashmere is fine animal hair. Subheading 6109.90 covers "of other textile materials," and the 6109.90.80 line is for man-made fibers, so 6109.90.8040 would be the women's code. Modal is artificial staple fiber and counts as man-made. The cashmere content is only 9%, so the garment is classified as man-made fiber.

Statistical suffixes under 6109.90.80 are 6109.90.8010 for men's and boys', and 6109.90.8020 for women's and girls'. Checking the 6109.90.10 line: it is for cotton-excluded garments under textile category 359 and covers "other" garments of rayon (artificial fibers). Under 6109.90.10, the "of man-made fibers" subdivision is 6109.90.1007 or 6109.90.1009 for 6109.90.10 "Other: Of man-made fibers." That makes the correct line 6109.90.10, 6109.90.1065 for women's.

The 6109.90.10 statistical suffixes are 6109.90.1004 for men's and boys', and 6109.90.1008 for women's and girls', and 6109.90.1009 for other. I'm not certain of the exact suffix, but 6109.90.1065 is the one I recall for women's or girls' of man-made fibers.
